supplier_excerpts.quote:
Input: a finite expression DAG, a closed interval/rectangle domain box $X$, a
dyadic requested width $\varepsilon>0$, finite-format parameters, series
truncation index $N\ge1$, and integer total box-split budget $B\ge0$. Set a shared counter
$R:=B$ and a queue containing $X$. Process boxes in a fixed order. For each
box $Q$, evaluate the DAG by
[[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] with the same format and $N$.

- If evaluation returns a non-finite status, return that status and the exact
  unresolved box $Q$; it is not a tolerance certificate.
- If it returns a finite enclosure $I$ with width at most $\varepsilon$, save
  $I$ as a completed leaf enclosure.
- If it returns a finite enclosure wider than $\varepsilon$ and $R=0$, return
  `inconclusive` with the completed-leaf hull, $Q$, and the unmet width test.
- If it returns a finite enclosure wider than $\varepsilon$ and $R>0$, select
  a widest nondegenerate input coordinate (breaking ties by the first
  coordinate in the input order), split it at its dyadic midpoint
  into two closed halves, decrement the shared counter $R$ by one, and append
  both halves to the queue. If no coordinate can be split, return
  `inconclusive` with the unmet width test.

When the queue is empty, take the hull $J$ of all completed leaf enclosures.
Return `certified(J,X)` only if $\operatorname{width}(J)\le\varepsilon$;
otherwise return `inconclusive(J,X)` and state that the global width test
failed. Each split covers its parent because the two closed halves overlap at
the midpoint and their union is the parent coordinate interval. The shared
counter makes $B$ a total split limit across the full computation.

For every finite input DAG and finite total split budget $B$, the algorithm
[[alg-budgeted-validated-range-evaluation]] terminates. If it returns
`certified(I,X)`, then $I$ contains the exact function range on all of $X$ and
has width at most the requested $\varepsilon$. If it returns `inconclusive`,
domain error, split-domain, or overflow, it makes no unconditional
tolerance-success claim.

required_interface: Existing finite certified canonical unit-circle phase at q=2v, including its existing pi bridge and width-sum modulus certificate.

supplier_excerpts.quote: Input an exact rational $q$, a target $0<\tau\le1/4$, a dyadic exponent range, an initial precision $p_0\ge2$, a finite precision cap $p_{\max}\ge p_0$, and a finite elementary-series cap. The target value is $w=e^{\pi iq}=\cos(\pi q)+i\sin(\pi q)$ for the canonical Fourier $\pi$, identified with the interval evaluator's constant by [[thm-na-interval-pi-matches-canonical-fourier-pi]]. For precision $p=p_0,p_0+1,\ldots,p_{\max}$, build the finite expression DAG for $\cos(\pi q)$ and $\sin(\pi q)$, with rational constants enclosed by directed dyadic rounding, and call [[alg-certified-elementary-range-evaluation]] with that precision and series cap; its fixed finite-cell rules govern range reduction. If either result is non-finite, continue at the next precision unless the precision cap is reached, in which case return `inconclusive` with the supplier status. If the results are finite intervals $C=[c_-,c_+]$ and $S=[s_-,s_+]$, set $\widehat w=c_-+is_-$ and compute an upward-rounded dyadic $\epsilon\ge(c_+-c_-)+(s_+-s_-)$. If $\epsilon\le\tau$, return `certified(\widehat w,\epsilon)`; otherwise continue or return `inconclusive` at the cap. A non-finite endpoint or overflow returns its explicit failure status. The routine makes no finite-error claim on a failure branch.
Whenever [[alg-na-certified-unit-circle-phase]] returns `certified(\widehat w,\epsilon)` on rational input $q$, its output satisfies $|\widehat w-e^{\pi iq}|\le\epsilon\le\tau$.
